sanskrit: satyaṃ bṛhad ṛtam ugraṃ dīkṣā tapo brahma yajñaḥ pṛthivīṃ dhārayanti | sā no bhūtasya bhavyasya patny uruṃ lokaṃ pṛthivī naḥ kṛṇotv asaṃbādhaṃ madhyato mānaveṣu ||
english: Truth, the vast, cosmic order fierce, consecration, austerity, sacred knowledge, and sacrifice — these uphold the Earth. She, the mistress of what has been and what shall be, may Earth make a wide world for us, unobstructed, in the midst of humankind.

sanskrit: yasyā udyataḥ pravataḥ samaṃ bahu nānāvīryā oṣadhīr yā bibharti | pṛthivī naḥ prathatāṃ rādhyatāṃ naḥ ||
english: She who bears the upland slopes, the plains, and the level stretches, the many-powered herbs — may Earth spread wide for us, may she prosper us.

sanskrit: yasyāṃ samudra uta sindhur āpo yasyāṃ devā anṛtam anvavindan | yā bibharti bahudhā prāṇam ejat sā no bhūmir goṣv aśveṣv apy anne kṛṇotu ||
english: She in whom the ocean, the river, and the waters dwell; she in whom the gods discovered the untruth; she who sustains in manifold ways the living breath that stirs — may that Earth bestow upon us cattle, horses, and food.

sanskrit: yasyāṃ pūrve pūrvajanā vicakrire yasyāṃ devā asurān abhyavartayan | yasyām idaṃ jīvati viśvam ejat sā no bhūmiḥ pūrvapeye dadhātu ||
english: She upon whom the ancestors of old moved about; she upon whom the gods turned back the asuras; she in whom all this living, stirring universe dwells — may that Earth grant us the first draft of life.

sanskrit: yasyāṃ catasraḥ pradiśaḥ pṛthivyāṃ yasyām annaṃ kṛṣṭayaḥ saṃbabhūvuḥ | gavām aśvānāṃ vayasaś ca viṣṭhā bhagaṃ varcaḥ pṛthivī no dadhātu ||
english: She in whom the four directions of Earth exist; she in whom food and cultivated peoples arose — the station of cattle, horses, and birds — may Earth grant us fortune and vital radiance.

sanskrit: viśvaṃbharā vasudhānī pratiṣṭhā hiraṇyavakṣā jagato niveśanīḥ | vaiśvānaraṃ bibhratī bhūmir agnim indrarṣabhā draviṇe no dadhātu ||
english: The all-sustaining, wealth-holding, steady foundation, golden-breasted resting place of the world — bearing Vaiśvānara, the universal fire, Earth, whose bull is Indra, may she bestow wealth upon us.

sanskrit: yasyām āpaḥ paricarāḥ samānīr ahorātre apramādaṃ kṣaranti | sā no bhūmir bhūridhārā payo duhām atho ukṣatu varcasā ||
english: She on whom the gathering waters flow in their rounds, pouring day and night without ceasing — may that Earth, abundant-streamed, milk nourishment for us, and also sprinkle us with vital radiance.

sanskrit: yāṃ rakṣanty asvapnā viśvadānīṃ devā bhūmiṃ pṛthivīm apramādam | sā no madhu priyaṃ duhām atho ukṣatu varcasā ||
english: She whom the gods guard, ever-wakeful, at all times, the Earth, the wide one, without negligence — may she milk sweet, dear nourishment for us, and also sprinkle us with vital radiance.

sanskrit: yārṇave 'dhi salilam agra āsīd yāṃ māyābhir anvacaran manīṣiṇaḥ | yasyāṃ hṛdayaṃ parame vyomant satyenāvṛtam amṛtaṃ pṛthivyāḥ | sā no bhūmis tviṣiṃ balaṃ rāṣṭre dadhātu me ||
english: She who was the primordial waters above the ocean; whom the wise have traced through their visionary powers; she whose heart, in the highest sky, is wrapped in truth, the immortal essence of Earth — may that Earth place brilliance and strength in my realm for me.

sanskrit: yām aśvināv amimātāṃ viṣṇur yasyāṃ vicakrame | indro yāṃ cakra ātmane anamitrāṃ chacīpatiḥ | sā no bhūmir vi sṛjatāṃ mātā putrāya naḥ payaḥ ||
english: She whom the two Aśvins measured out, upon whom Viṣṇu strode; she whom Indra, lord of power, made enemy-free for himself — may that Earth release milk for us as a mother for her son.

sanskrit: girayas te parvatā himavanto 'raṇyan te pṛthivi syonam astu naḥ | babhruṃ kṛṣṇāṃ rohiṇīṃ viśvarūpāṃ dhruvāṃ bhūmiṃ pṛthivīm indraguptām ajīto 'hato akṣato adhyaṣṭhāṃ pṛthivīm aham ||
english: Your hills, your mountains, your snow-bearing ranges, your forests, O Earth — may it be gentle for us. I stand upon the tawny, black, reddish, all-formed, firm Earth, protected by Indra — unconquered, unslain, unwounded, I take my stand upon the Earth.

sanskrit: yat te madhyaṃ pṛthivi yac ca nabhyaṃ yās ta ūrjas tanvaḥ saṃbabhūvuḥ | tāsu no dhehy abhi naḥ pavasva ||
english: What is your center, O Earth, what is your navel, and those bodily energies that have arisen from you — set us there, purify us.

sanskrit: mātā bhūmiḥ putro ahaṃ pṛthivyāḥ parjanyaḥ pitā sa u naḥ pipartu ||
english: Earth is the mother, I am the son of Earth; Parjanya is the father — may he fill us with nourishment.

sanskrit: yasyāṃ vediṃ parigṛhnanti bhūmyāṃ yasyāṃ yajñaṃ tanvate viśvakarmāṇaḥ | yasyāṃ mīyante svaravaḥ pṛthivyām ūrdhvāḥ śukrā āhutyāḥ purastāt | sā no bhūmir vardhayād vardhamānā ||
english: She on whose surface they set up the altar, on whom the all-skilled ones spread out the sacrifice; she on whose surface the wooden stakes are measured out, and the bright oblations ascend before — may that growing Earth increase us.

sanskrit: yo no dveṣat pṛthivi yat pṛtanyād yo 'bhimanyātai manasā vadhena | tan no bhūme randhaya pūrvakṛtvane ||
english: Whoever hates us, O Earth, whoever attacks us, whoever with his mind intends to slay us — deliver that one to us, O Earth, as you have done in former times.

sanskrit: tvajjātās tvayi caranti martyās tvaṃ bibharṣi dvipadaś catuṣpadaḥ | tvayīme pṛthivi pañca mānavā yebhyo jyotir amṛtaṃ martyebhya udyan sūryo raśmibhir ā tanoti ||
english: Born from you, mortals move about on you; you sustain the two-footed and the four-footed. In you, O Earth, are these five races of humans, for whom the rising sun stretches out the immortal light with its rays to mortal beings.

sanskrit: tā naḥ prajāḥ saṃ duhratāṃ samagrā vāco madhu pṛthivī dhehi mahyam ||
english: May all those offspring be milked for us completely; O Earth, place the sweetness of speech in me.

sanskrit: viśvasvaṃ mātaram oṣadhīnāṃ dhruvāṃ bhūmiṃ pṛthivīṃ dharmaṇā dhṛtām | śivāṃ syonām anu carema viśvahā ||
english: The mother of all, of herbs, the firm Earth, the wide one, held firm by cosmic law — may we ever walk in her, benign and gentle, all our days.

sanskrit: mahat sadhasthaṃ mahatī babhūvitha mahān vega ejathur vepathuṣ ṭe | mahāṃs tvendro rakṣati vīryeṇa sā no bhūme prarocaya hiraṇyasyeva saṃdṛśi ||
english: Great is your assembly place; you have become great; great is the speed, your trembling, your quaking. Great Indra guards you with his might — O Earth, make us glorious in sight, as though shining with gold.

sanskrit: agnir bhūmyām agnir oṣadhīṣv agnim āpo bibhraty agnir aśmasu | agnir antaḥ puruṣeṣu goṣv aśveṣv agnayaḥ ||
english: Fire is in the Earth, fire is in the herbs; the waters carry fire, fire is in the stones. Fire is within human beings; fires are in cattle and horses.

sanskrit: agnir diva ā tapaty agner devasyorv antarikṣam | agniṃ martāsa indhate havyavāhaṃ ghṛtapriyam ||
english: Fire blazes from the sky; from divine Fire comes the broad atmosphere. Mortals kindle Fire, the carrier of oblations, the lover of clarified butter.

sanskrit: agnivāsāḥ pṛthivy asitajñus tviṣīmantaṃ saṃśitaṃ mā kṛṇotu | bhūmyāṃ devebhyo juhvati yajñaṃ havyam araṃkṛtam | bhūmyāṃ manuṣyā jīvanti svadhayānnena martyāḥ | sā no bhūmiḥ prāṇam āyur dadhātu jaradaṣṭiṃ mā pṛthivī kṛṇotu ||
english: Earth, the abode of fire, dark-kneed — may she not make me shrunken, wasted, or without brilliance. On the Earth they pour out the sacrifice, the duly prepared oblation, for the gods. On the Earth mortals live, sustained by food according to their nature. May that Earth grant us breath and long life; may Earth not make us bitten by old age.

sanskrit: yas te gandhaḥ pṛthivi saṃbabhūva yaṃ bibhraty oṣadhayo yam āpaḥ | yaṃ gandharvā apsarasaś ca bhejire yas te gām aśvam arhati | tenāsmān surabhīn kṛṇu mā no dvikṣata kaś cana ||
english: That fragrance of yours, O Earth, which has arisen, which the herbs carry, which the waters carry, which the gandharvas and apsarases have shared, which befits a cow and a horse — with that make us fragrant; let no one hate us.

sanskrit: yas te gandhaḥ puṣkaram āviveśa yaṃ saṃjabhruḥ sūryāyā vivāhe | amartyāḥ pṛthivi gandham agre | tenāsmān surabhīn kṛṇu mā no dvikṣata kaś cana ||
english: That fragrance of yours which entered the lotus, which was gathered at the wedding of Sūryā — the immortals, O Earth, took the fragrance first. With that make us fragrant; let no one hate us.

sanskrit: yas te bhūme puruṣeṣu strīṣu puṃsu bhago rucir yo vadhūṣu vadhūyuṣu | yo goṣv aśveṣu yo mṛgeṣūta hastiṣu | kanyāyāṃ varco yad bhūme tenāsmām̐ adhi saṃ sṛja mā no dvikṣata kaś cana ||
english: That lustre and splendor of yours, O Earth, which is in men and in women, which is in brides and in bridegrooms, which is in cattle and horses, in wild beasts, and in elephants — that vital radiance which is in a maiden, O Earth — with that unite us; let no one hate us.

sanskrit: śilā bhūmir aśmā pāṃsur yā bhūmiḥ saṃbhṛtā dhṛtā | yasyāṃ vṛkṣā vānaspatyā dhruvās tiṣṭhanti viśvahā | bhūmiṃ hiraṇyavakṣasaṃ dhṛtām acchā vadāmasi ||
english: Rock, Earth, stone, sand — the Earth that has been gathered together and held firm; she on whose surface the forest trees stand firm forever — to that golden-breasted, steadily held Earth we address our words.

sanskrit: udīrāṇā utāsīnās tiṣṭhantaḥ prakrāmantaḥ | padbhyāṃ dakṣiṇasavyābhyāṃ mā vyathiṣmahi bhūmyām ||
english: Rising, sitting, standing, walking about — may we not stumble upon the Earth with our right and left feet.

sanskrit: vimṛgvarīṃ pṛthivīm ā vadāmi kṣamāṃ bhūmiṃ brahmaṇā vāvṛdhānām | ūrjaṃ puṣṭiṃ bibhratīm annabhāgaṃ ghṛtaṃ tvābhi ni ṣīdāmi bhūme ||
english: I address the wide Earth, the patient Earth, the ground swelling with sacred power, bearing vigor, nourishment, and a share of food — upon you, O Earth, upon clarified butter, I take my seat.

sanskrit: śuddhā ma āpas tanvaḥ kṣaranti yo me sehur apriye taṃ ni dadhmaḥ | pavitreṇa pṛthivīm ut punāmi ||
english: May pure waters flow over my body; whoever my foe is in what is not dear to me, him I lay low. With the purifying strainer I purify the Earth.

sanskrit: nidhīn bibhratī bahudhā guhā vasu maṇiṃ hiraṇyaṃ pṛthivī dadhātu naḥ | vasūni no vasudā rāsamānā devī dadhātu sumanasyamānā ||
english: Bearing treasures in many hidden places — gems, gold — may Earth bestow wealth on us. The goddess, wealth-giving, graciously bestowing, of good mind, may she grant us riches.
